In preparation for reworking the usb_get_device_descriptor() routine
it is desirable to unite the two different code paths responsible for
initially determining endpoint 0's maximum packet size in a newly
discovered USB device.  Making this determination presents a
chicken-and-egg sort of problem
column2: in that the only way to learn the

column1: maxpacket value is to get it from the device descriptor retrieved from
the device
column2: but communicating with the device to retrieve a descriptor

column1: requires us to know beforehand the ep0 maxpacket size.
In practice this problem is solved in two different ways
in hub.c as the ""old scheme"" and the ""new scheme"".  The old scheme
(which is the approach recommended by the USB-2 spec) involves asking
the device to send just the first eight bytes of its device
descriptor.  Such a transfer uses packets containing no more than
eight bytes each
column2: and every USB device must have an ep0 maxpacket size
so this should succeed.  Since the bMaxPacketSize0 field of the

column1: device descriptor lies within the first eight bytes
need.
The new scheme is an imitation of the technique used in an early
Windows USB implementation
column2: giving it the happy advantage of working

column1: with a wide variety of devices (some of them at the time would not
work with the old scheme
column2: although that's probably less true now).  It

column1: involves making an initial guess of the ep0 maxpacket size
device to send up to 64 bytes worth of its device descriptor (which is
only 18 bytes long)
column2: and then resetting the device to clear any error

column1: condition that might have resulted from the guess being wrong.  The
initial guess is determined by the connection speed; it should be
correct in all cases other than full speed
values are 8
column4: and 64 (in this case the initial guess is 64).

column1: The reason for this patch is that the old- and new-scheme parts of
hub_port_init() use different code paths
usb_get_device_descriptor() and one not
the device descriptor.  Since these reads have essentially the same
purpose and are made under essentially the same circumstances
illogical.  It makes more sense to have both of them use a common
subroutine.
This subroutine does basically what the new scheme's code did
that approach is more general than the one used by the old scheme.  It
only needs to know how many bytes to transfer and whether or not it is
being called for the first iteration of a retry loop (in case of
certain time-out errors).  There are two main differences from the
former code:
We initialize the bDescriptorType field of the transfer buffer
to 0 before performing the transfer
accessing an uninitialized value afterward.
We read the device descriptor into a temporary buffer rather
than storing it directly into udev->descriptor
scheme implementation used to do.
Since the whole point of this first read of the device descriptor is
to determine the bMaxPacketSize0 value
column2: that is what the new routine

column1: returns (or an error code).  The value is stored in a local variable
rather than in udev->descriptor.  As a side effect
moving a section of code that checks the bcdUSB field for SuperSpeed
devices until after the full device descriptor has been retrieved.
